reconcile.note: Gill treats Luke's perplexity and Mark's firm identification as successive stages of one process, as Herod's doubt hardened into conviction under his guilty conscience.

discrepancy.note: Strauss records Herod's flat identification of Jesus as the risen John, the position Luke's Herod does not share.

quotes.text: where Herod, on hearing of the miracles of Jesus, says: It is John the Baptist, he is risen from the dead.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), §100 n.24, on Matthew 14:2.

sides.snippet: This is John, whom I beheaded. He has risen from the dead.
sides.verseText: But Herod, when he heard this, said, \"This is John, whom I beheaded. He has risen from the dead.\"

sides.snippet: John I beheaded, but who is this, about whom I hear such things?
sides.verseText: Herod said, \"John I beheaded, but who is this, about whom I hear such things?\" He sought to see him.
